# Introduction

GeneFunnel turns a non-negative feature-by-sample matrix into a
gene-set-by-sample score matrix. It preserves observed magnitude while
penalizing absolute variation among the available members of each set. Every
gene set and sample is calculated independently.

Transcriptomic and proteomic assays commonly use Bioconductor's matrix,
sparse-matrix, and parallel infrastructure. GeneFunnel fits that environment by
accepting base and `Matrix` matrices and a `BiocParallelParam`, while returning
a plain numeric matrix for downstream analysis. It is a scorer only: it does
not normalize data, impute missing values, map identifiers, retrieve gene sets,
or perform statistical testing.

Within a larger pipeline, GeneFunnel can follow assay-specific preprocessing,
identifier mapping, and coverage checks. Its output can then provide
gene-set-level features for sample prioritization, visualization, clustering, or
statistical models.

The package is in development and has not been accepted into Bioconductor. Its
source and issue tracker are on the
[GeneFunnel repository](https://github.com/eturkes/genefunnel).

# Installation

After acceptance, install GeneFunnel from a Bioconductor package repository:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("genefunnel")
```

During review, replace the package name with `"eturkes/genefunnel"` to install
the development repository.

Load the installed package and choose a serial backend for the first examples.

```{r load}
library(genefunnel)
serial <- BiocParallel::SerialParam()
```

# How the score is calculated

For one declared gene set, GeneFunnel first deduplicates member identifiers and
matches them exactly and case-sensitively to matrix row names. Within sample
$j$, it omits matched values that are `NA` or `NaN`. If the remaining observed
values are $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and $n \ge 2$, the score is

$$
\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{GeneFunnel}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
-\frac{n}{2(n-1)}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i-\bar{x}|.
$$

The cell is `NA_real_` when fewer than two observed members remain. Zero is an
observed value, including an implicit sparse zero, so it participates in $n$,
the sum, the mean, and the deviation. Infinities and negative values are
invalid.

The controlled panel below follows the exploratory logic used to motivate the
method. It holds total signal constant while changing within-set dispersion, and
it distinguishes observed zeros from unavailable measurements.

# Controlled expression patterns

Ten features form two five-member modules and one broader program. The six
samples represent deliberately different expression patterns rather than
biological replicates.

```{r controlled-patterns}
pattern_assay <- rbind(
    gene_A = c(38, 0, 80, 80, 80, 80),
    gene_B = c(41, 0, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_C = c(39, 92, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_D = c(42, 4, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_E = c(40, 112, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_F = c(37, 82, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_G = c(43, 5, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_H = c(40, 18, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_I = c(41, 85, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_J = c(39, 2, 80, NA, 0, 0)
)
colnames(pattern_assay) <- c(
    "coherent",
    "same_total_dispersed",
    "uniform_high",
    "partial_observation",
    "half_active",
    "single_driver"
)
pattern_sets <- list(
    module_A = rownames(pattern_assay)[1:5],
    module_B = rownames(pattern_assay)[6:10],
    broad_program = rownames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_assay,
    pattern_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

knitr::kable(
    pattern_assay,
    digits = 0,
    col.names = c(
        "Coherent",
        "Same total, dispersed",
        "Uniform high",
        "Partial observation",
        "Half active",
        "Single driver"
    )
)
```

```{r controlled-pattern-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.cap=pattern_heatmap_caption}
pattern_heatmap <- data.frame(
    feature = rep(rownames(pattern_assay), times = ncol(pattern_assay)),
    pattern = rep(colnames(pattern_assay), each = nrow(pattern_assay)),
    value = as.vector(pattern_assay),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
pattern_heatmap$feature <- factor(
    pattern_heatmap$feature,
    levels = rev(rownames(pattern_assay))
)
pattern_heatmap$pattern <- factor(
    pattern_heatmap$pattern,
    levels = colnames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_labels <- c(
    coherent = "Coherent",
    same_total_dispersed = "Same total,\ndispersed",
    uniform_high = "Uniform\nhigh",
    partial_observation = "Partial\nobservation",
    half_active = "Half\nactive",
    single_driver = "Single\ndriver"
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    pattern_heatmap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = feature, fill = value)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = pattern_heatmap[is.na(pattern_heatmap$value), , drop = FALSE],
        mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = feature),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 4,
        size = 2.1,
        stroke = 0.7,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = pattern_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF",
        high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        name = "Observed\nvalue"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Feature") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
        legend.position = "right"
    )
```

The following diagnostics expose the calculation for the broad program. The
scaled deviation is the complete penalty subtracted from the observed total.

```{r controlled-pattern-diagnostics}
pattern_diagnostics <- t(vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(pattern_assay)),
    function(column_index) {
        observed <- pattern_assay[, column_index]
        observed <- observed[!is.na(observed)]
        member_count <- length(observed)
        total <- sum(observed)
        average <- mean(observed)
        scaled_deviation <- member_count / (2 * (member_count - 1)) *
            sum(abs(observed - average))

        c(
            observed_members = member_count,
            total = total,
            mean = average,
            scaled_deviation = scaled_deviation,
            genefunnel_score =
                pattern_scores["broad_program", column_index]
        )
    },
    numeric(5L)
))
pattern_diagnostics <- data.frame(
    pattern = colnames(pattern_assay),
    pattern_diagnostics,
    check.names = FALSE
)
rownames(pattern_diagnostics) <- NULL
knitr::kable(
    pattern_diagnostics,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Pattern",
        "Observed members",
        "Total",
        "Mean",
        "Scaled deviation",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    unname(pattern_scores["broad_program", ]),
    c(3530 / 9, 1490 / 9, 800, 400, 1600 / 9, 0),
    tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```

```{r controlled-pattern-components, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap=pattern_components_caption}
pattern_components <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        pattern = pattern_diagnostics$pattern,
        component = "GeneFunnel score",
        fraction = pattern_diagnostics$genefunnel_score /
            pattern_diagnostics$total
    ),
    data.frame(
        pattern = pattern_diagnostics$pattern,
        component = "Deviation penalty",
        fraction = pattern_diagnostics$scaled_deviation /
            pattern_diagnostics$total
    )
)
pattern_components$pattern <- factor(
    pattern_components$pattern,
    levels = colnames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_components$component <- factor(
    pattern_components$component,
    levels = c("Deviation penalty", "GeneFunnel score")
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    pattern_components,
    ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = fraction, fill = component)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.72) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = pattern_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 1),
        breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
        labels = function(value) paste0(round(100 * value), "%"),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            "Deviation penalty" = "#D9D9D9",
            "GeneFunnel score" = "#2C7FB8"
        ),
        name = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of observed total") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
        legend.position = "top"
    )
```

The coherent and dispersed samples each total 400. The coherent sample has only
small feature-to-feature differences, so its score remains close to 400. The
dispersed sample contains the same total in a mixture of high values and zeros;
its larger deviation penalty reduces the score to 165.6.

The uniformly high sample has no deviation and therefore scores its full total
of 800. The partial-observation sample contains five observed values of 80 and
five `NA` values. GeneFunnel omits the unavailable values, uses an effective set
size of five, and scores the observed total of 400. In contrast, the zeros in the
half-active and single-driver samples remain observed evidence. Half activation
receives partial credit, while one non-zero feature among nine zeros gives the
maximally dispersed score of zero.

# A narrower set can explain partial activity

The same panel can be scored against nested definitions. In the half-active
sample, every member of module A is measured at 80, while every member of module
B is zero.

```{r nested-sets}
nested_comparison <- data.frame(
    gene_set = rownames(pattern_scores),
    half_active_score = unname(pattern_scores[, "half_active"]),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    nested_comparison,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Gene set", "Score in half-active sample")
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    nested_comparison$half_active_score,
    c(400, 0, 1600 / 9),
    tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```

Module A scores its full total, module B scores zero, and the broader program is
penalized because only half of its members are active. This mirrors a useful
interpretive property of the method: a specific active module can explain a
partial signal better than an encompassing set. The sets should still be
predeclared. The example is not a reason to search adaptively for whichever
subset gives the largest score.

# Controlled gene-set perturbations

A second experiment separates two changes that can produce a higher score. It
starts from one synthetic sample and makes a modified copy. For the six-member
assembly set, the modified values are all set to their original mean. Its total
stays fixed while its within-set variation disappears. For the five-member
receptor set, every value increases by 40 while its variation stays unchanged.
Three background features are not members of either primary set.

```{r controlled-perturbations}
assembly_members <- paste0("assembly_", seq_len(6L))
receptor_members <- paste0("receptor_", seq_len(5L))
background_members <- paste0("background_", seq_len(3L))

original_values <- c(
    setNames(c(10, 25, 40, 55, 70, 100), assembly_members),
    setNames(c(28, 31, 30, 29, 32), receptor_members),
    setNames(c(18, 44, 65), background_members)
)
modified_values <- original_values
modified_values[assembly_members] <- mean(original_values[assembly_members])
modified_values[receptor_members] <-
    original_values[receptor_members] + 40

perturbation_assay <- cbind(
    original = original_values,
    modified = modified_values
)
perturbation_sets <- list(
    complex_assembly = assembly_members,
    receptor_activity = receptor_members,
    overlapping_response = c(
        assembly_members[5:6],
        receptor_members[1:3]
    )
)
perturbation_scores <- genefunnel(
    perturbation_assay,
    perturbation_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

knitr::kable(
    perturbation_assay,
    digits = 0,
    col.names = c("Original", "Modified")
)
```

```{r controlled-perturbation-diagnostics}
perturbation_diagnostics <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(perturbation_sets), function(set_name) {
        members <- perturbation_sets[[set_name]]
        totals <- colSums(perturbation_assay[members, , drop = FALSE])
        scores <- perturbation_scores[set_name, ]

        data.frame(
            gene_set = set_name,
            sample = colnames(perturbation_assay),
            total = unname(totals),
            scaled_deviation = unname(totals - scores),
            genefunnel_score = unname(scores),
            check.names = FALSE
        )
    })
)
rownames(perturbation_diagnostics) <- NULL
knitr::kable(
    perturbation_diagnostics,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Gene set",
        "Sample",
        "Total",
        "Scaled deviation",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)

stopifnot(
    identical(
        unname(colSums(perturbation_assay[assembly_members, ])),
        c(300, 300)
    ),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(perturbation_scores["complex_assembly", ]),
        c(210, 300),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(perturbation_scores["receptor_activity", ]),
        c(146.25, 346.25),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    ))
)
```

```{r controlled-perturbation-benchmark, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap=perturbation_benchmark_caption}
perturbation_plot <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        gene_set = perturbation_diagnostics$gene_set,
        sample = perturbation_diagnostics$sample,
        metric = "Observed total",
        value = perturbation_diagnostics$total
    ),
    data.frame(
        gene_set = perturbation_diagnostics$gene_set,
        sample = perturbation_diagnostics$sample,
        metric = "GeneFunnel score",
        value = perturbation_diagnostics$genefunnel_score
    )
)
perturbation_plot$sample <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$sample,
    levels = c("original", "modified"),
    labels = c("Original", "Modified")
)
perturbation_plot$metric <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$metric,
    levels = c("Observed total", "GeneFunnel score")
)
perturbation_plot$gene_set <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$gene_set,
    levels = names(perturbation_sets),
    labels = c(
        "Complex assembly",
        "Receptor activity",
        "Overlapping response"
    )
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    perturbation_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = value, fill = metric)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(
        position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.72),
        width = 0.65
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(gene_set), nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            "Observed total" = "#BDBDBD",
            "GeneFunnel score" = "#2C7FB8"
        ),
        name = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Value") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top"
    )
```

The assembly score rises from 210 to 300 without any change in its total. The
change is entirely due to greater coherence. The receptor score rises by 200
because its total rises by 200 and its deviation penalty remains 3.75. The
overlapping response also changes because it shares members with both modified
sets, but every set is still calculated independently.

This controlled design reflects two questions that appear in practical
analyses: did the members move together, and did their combined magnitude
change? GeneFunnel can register either effect in its sample-wise score. A
subsequent model is still required to estimate uncertainty or test differences
between biological groups.

# Real-data case study: NFT-bearing neurons

The thesis applied GeneFunnel to molecular changes in neurofibrillary
tangle-bearing neurons. A public component of that work reanalysed
[GSE129308](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE129308), the
single-soma transcriptomic study reported by
[Otero-Garcia et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2022.06.021). The study
paired AT8-sorted NFT-bearing neurons with neighbouring MAP2-sorted NFT-free
neurons from eight Braak stage VI Alzheimer's disease donors.

Package vignettes must build without downloading hundreds of megabytes. The
installed fixture therefore contains selected-gene UMI totals aggregated from
the 16 deposited Cell Ranger-filtered matrices. It records one MAP2 and one AT8
aggregate per donor, together with the number of deposited barcodes and total
library size. The source repository includes a checksum-verified regeneration
script under `data-raw/`.

The compact workflow below converts each aggregate to counts per million and
then calculates `log2(CPM + 1)`. This preserves non-negative values while
adjusting for library size. The full thesis workflow instead scored individual
somas before donor-level pseudobulk aggregation and included additional quality
control. This vignette is a practical package example, not a reproduction of
that analysis.

Four illustrative panels connect the fixture to thesis themes. The first uses
the eight hub genes prioritised in the integrated analysis. The others sample
protein-folding, postsynaptic-structure, and synaptic-vesicle biology discussed
there. They are compact teaching panels, not canonical ontology definitions.

```{r gse129308-data}
gse129308_gene_sets <- list(
    thesis_hubs = c(
        "NEFM", "APP", "SQSTM1", "HSP90AA1",
        "YWHAE", "WASF1", "CNTNAP1", "GOT2"
    ),
    protein_folding = c(
        "HSP90AA1", "HSP90AB1", "HSPA8", "CCT2", "CCT3", "CCT4",
        "CCT5", "CCT6A", "CCT7", "CCT8", "TCP1"
    ),
    postsynaptic_structure = c(
        "NEFM", "WASF1", "CNTNAP1", "DLG4", "SHANK1", "SHANK2",
        "SHANK3", "ACTB", "TUBB", "TUBB3"
    ),
    synaptic_vesicle_release = c("SYN1", "SYP", "SNAP25", "STX1A", "VAMP2")
)
gse129308_genes <- unique(unlist(gse129308_gene_sets, use.names = FALSE))
gse129308_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "GSE129308_AD_pseudobulk_counts.csv",
    package = "genefunnel"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(gse129308_path))
gse129308 <- utils::read.csv(
    gse129308_path,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
stopifnot(all(gse129308_genes %in% names(gse129308)))

gse129308_counts <- t(as.matrix(
    gse129308[, gse129308_genes, drop = FALSE]
))
colnames(gse129308_counts) <- gse129308$sample
storage.mode(gse129308_counts) <- "double"
gse129308_cpm <- sweep(
    gse129308_counts,
    2L,
    gse129308$library_size,
    "/"
) * 1e6
gse129308_expression <- log2(gse129308_cpm + 1)

gse129308_coverage <- gene_set_coverage(
    gse129308_gene_sets,
    rownames(gse129308_expression)
)
knitr::kable(
    gse129308_coverage,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Panel",
        "Declared",
        "Matched",
        "Unmatched",
        "Coverage",
        "Duplicates",
        "Scoreable"
    )
)

gse129308_scores <- genefunnel(
    gse129308_expression,
    gse129308_gene_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)
```

The fixture has complete identifier coverage for these declared panels. The
scores can therefore be reshaped into paired donor trajectories without any
sample-specific member loss.

```{r gse129308-summary}
gse129308_panel_labels <- c(
    thesis_hubs = "Thesis hubs",
    protein_folding = "Protein folding",
    postsynaptic_structure = "Postsynaptic structure",
    synaptic_vesicle_release = "Synaptic vesicle release"
)
gse129308_score_long <- data.frame(
    panel = rep(rownames(gse129308_scores), times = ncol(gse129308_scores)),
    sample = rep(colnames(gse129308_scores), each = nrow(gse129308_scores)),
    score = as.vector(gse129308_scores),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
gse129308_sample_index <- match(
    gse129308_score_long$sample,
    gse129308$sample
)
gse129308_score_long$donor <- gse129308$donor[gse129308_sample_index]
gse129308_score_long$sort_marker <-
    gse129308$sort_marker[gse129308_sample_index]

gse129308_summary <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(gse129308_gene_sets), function(panel_name) {
        panel_data <- gse129308_score_long[
            gse129308_score_long$panel == panel_name,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]
        donors <- sort(unique(panel_data$donor))
        map2_scores <- vapply(
            donors,
            function(donor) {
                panel_data$score[
                    panel_data$donor == donor &
                        panel_data$sort_marker == "MAP2"
                ]
            },
            numeric(1L)
        )
        at8_scores <- vapply(
            donors,
            function(donor) {
                panel_data$score[
                    panel_data$donor == donor &
                        panel_data$sort_marker == "AT8"
                ]
            },
            numeric(1L)
        )
        data.frame(
            panel = unname(gse129308_panel_labels[[panel_name]]),
            matched_members = gse129308_coverage$matched_size[
                match(panel_name, gse129308_coverage$gene_set)
            ],
            mean_map2 = mean(map2_scores),
            mean_at8 = mean(at8_scores),
            mean_paired_difference = mean(at8_scores - map2_scores),
            at8_higher_donors = sprintf(
                "%d / %d",
                sum(at8_scores > map2_scores),
                length(donors)
            ),
            check.names = FALSE
        )
    })
)
rownames(gse129308_summary) <- NULL
knitr::kable(
    gse129308_summary,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Panel",
        "Matched members",
        "Mean MAP2 score",
        "Mean AT8 score",
        "Mean paired difference",
        "Donors with AT8 > MAP2"
    )
)
```

```{r gse129308-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.8, fig.cap=gse129308_caption}
gse129308_score_long$population <- factor(
    gse129308_score_long$sort_marker,
    levels = c("MAP2", "AT8"),
    labels = c("NFT-free (MAP2)", "NFT-bearing (AT8)")
)
gse129308_score_long$panel <- factor(
    gse129308_score_long$panel,
    levels = names(gse129308_panel_labels),
    labels = unname(gse129308_panel_labels)
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    gse129308_score_long,
    ggplot2::aes(x = population, y = score, group = donor)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#8C8C8C", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        ggplot2::aes(fill = population),
        shape = 21,
        size = 2.4,
        colour = "#333333"
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(panel), ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            "NFT-free (MAP2)" = "#4477AA",
            "NFT-bearing (AT8)" = "#CC6677"
        ),
        guide = "none"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "GeneFunnel score") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)
    )
```

```{r gse129308-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
    identical(dim(gse129308_counts), c(30L, 16L)),
    identical(
        as.integer(table(gse129308$sort_marker)[c("MAP2", "AT8")]),
        c(8L, 8L)
    ),
    all(gse129308_coverage$coverage == 1),
    identical(
        gse129308_summary$at8_higher_donors,
        c("8 / 8", "7 / 8", "8 / 8", "7 / 8")
    ),
    all(gse129308_summary$mean_paired_difference > 0)
)
```

The selected hub and postsynaptic panels score higher in every paired AT8
aggregate. The other two panels show the same direction in seven of eight
donors. This example adds realistic donor variation and assay scale to the
controlled demonstrations. It does not establish differential pathway activity:
the panels were selected for illustration, the aggregate differs from the full
thesis pipeline, and no inferential model is fitted here.

# Choosing between GeneFunnel and rank-based methods

Gene-set scoring is already supported by several complementary packages.
[`GSVA`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GSVA) offers unsupervised gene-set
transformations whose methods use relative expression or rank information.
[`singscore`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/singscore) and
[`UCell`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/UCell) calculate single-sample
scores from within-sample feature ranks, with UCell using a Mann-Whitney U
statistic.

GeneFunnel answers a different question. It does not rank values or estimate a
distribution across samples. Instead, it applies the formula above to each set
and sample independently. The score therefore depends on measurement scale,
set size, and observed coverage. Choose the method that matches the quantity
you want to preserve.

# Check coverage before scoring

A declared member absent from the matrix changes global assay coverage. It is
different from a missing cell, which affects only one sample, and from an
observed zero. `gene_set_coverage()` exposes these facts before scoring.

```{r coverage}
catalogue <- list(
    complete_module = rownames(pattern_assay)[1:5],
    partial_catalogue = c("gene_A", "gene_B", "gene_C", "gene_K"),
    duplicated_members = c("gene_A", "gene_A", "gene_B"),
    insufficient = c("gene_A", "gene_Z")
)
coverage <- gene_set_coverage(catalogue, rownames(pattern_assay))
knitr::kable(
    coverage,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Gene set",
        "Declared",
        "Matched",
        "Unmatched",
        "Coverage",
        "Duplicates",
        "Scoreable"
    )
)
```

GeneFunnel can score a set whenever at least two unique members match. It does
not impose a coverage fraction because suitable thresholds depend on the
experiment. A transcriptomic analysis might require complete coverage:

```{r strict-coverage}
strict <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) & coverage$coverage == 1
names(catalogue[strict])
```

A low-coverage proteomic analysis might require at least 50% coverage and at
least two matched members:

```{r relaxed-coverage}
relaxed <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) &
    coverage$coverage >= 0.5 &
    coverage$matched_size >= 2
names(catalogue[relaxed])

relaxed_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_assay,
    catalogue[relaxed],
    BPPARAM = serial
)
knitr::kable(
    relaxed_scores,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Coherent",
        "Same total, dispersed",
        "Uniform high",
        "Partial observation",
        "Half active",
        "Single driver"
    )
)
```

These thresholds are examples rather than package recommendations. Record the
gene-set collection, its version, and the threshold used in the analysis.

# Dense and sparse matrices

Sparse input stays sparse through scoring, and implicit zeros remain observed.
Stored sparse `NA` and `NaN` values follow the same sample-specific omission
rule as dense missing values.

```{r sparse}
pattern_sparse <- Matrix::Matrix(pattern_assay, sparse = TRUE)
pattern_sparse_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_sparse,
    pattern_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

isTRUE(all.equal(
    pattern_sparse_scores,
    pattern_scores,
    tolerance = 0,
    check.attributes = TRUE
))
```

The dense and sparse implementations are required to produce the same named
matrix. Sparse storage changes memory use and traversal, not the scientific
calculation.

# Serial and parallel execution

`BPPARAM` accepts any suitable `BiocParallelParam`. `SerialParam()` is useful
for debugging and small inputs. A portable SOCK backend can distribute bounded
column chunks while preserving sample order.

```{r parallel}
sock <- BiocParallel::bpstart(BiocParallel::SnowParam(
    workers = 2L,
    type = "SOCK",
    progressbar = FALSE
))
parallel_scores <- tryCatch(
    genefunnel(pattern_assay, pattern_sets, BPPARAM = sock),
    finally = BiocParallel::bpstop(sock)
)

identical(parallel_scores, pattern_scores)
```

Process startup and data transfer can outweigh parallel work on small inputs.
Benchmark the intended workload rather than assuming that more workers are
faster.

# Identifiers and preprocessing

Matrix row names and gene-set names must be unique, non-missing, and non-empty.
Member matching is exact, with no case conversion, synonym resolution, or
annotation lookup. Duplicated members within one set are counted in coverage
diagnostics and deduplicated for scoring. Overlapping sets remain valid and do
not influence one another.

GeneFunnel requires non-negative input with a meaningful zero. It applies no
automatic preprocessing. An arbitrary positive shift is unsuitable because
adding a constant $c$ to all $n$ observed members adds $nc$ to the score. Raw
non-negative measurements can be preferable when scientifically appropriate,
but the package does not prescribe a universal pipeline position.

# Interpretation and limitations

The absolute-deviation penalty treats within-set variability as evidence
against coherent activity. That is a scientific assumption rather than a
universal property of biological pathways.

The sum term preserves magnitude and therefore also preserves effects of input
units, library size, preprocessing, set size, and feature coverage. Independent
sample scoring does not make scores from unrelated data sets automatically
comparable. Such comparisons require compatible units, preprocessing,
identifiers, gene-set definitions, versions, and coverage policies.

Gene-set database revisions can change scores. The package does not guarantee
that the resulting distribution meets the assumptions of every downstream
statistical method. Validate those assumptions for the intended analysis.

The full scoring specification is installed as `SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md`:

```{r specification-path}
specification <- system.file("SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md", package = "genefunnel")
stopifnot(nzchar(specification), file.exists(specification))
basename(specification)
```
